questions.q: Three blocks $A, B$ and $C$ are pulled on a horizontal smooth surface by a force of $80N$ as shown in figure. The tensions ${T}_{1}\text{and}{T}_{2}$ in the string are respectively:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Since, the length of the string will remain same. Hence, all blocks will have the same acceleration.

${a}_{A} = {a}_{B} = {a}_{C} = \dfrac{F}{5 + 3 + 2} = \dfrac{80}{10} = 8ms^{- 2}$

Therefore, ${T}_{1} = 5 \times 8 = 40N$.

Now,

${T}_{2} - {T}_{1} = 3 \times 8 ⇒ {T}_{2} = 64N$

questions.q: If two similar springs each of spring constant ${K}_{1}$ are joined in series, the new spring constant and time period would be changed by a factor:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{1}{keq} = \dfrac{1}{k1} + \dfrac{1}{k2}$

$\dfrac{1}{keq} = \dfrac{1}{k} + \dfrac{1}{k} ⇒ {k}_{eq} = \dfrac{k}{2}$

$k^{'} = \dfrac{k}{2}$

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{M}{k}}$

$T^{'} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{M}{k '}}$

$⇒ T^{'} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{M}{k}} \times \sqrt{2}$

$T^{'} = \sqrt{2}T$

questions.q:
A block of mass $40$ kg slides over a surface, when a mass of $4$ kg is suspended through an inextensible massless string passing over frictionless pulley as shown below.
The coefficient of kinetic friction between the surface and block is $0 . 02$. The acceleration of block is:~(Given $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$.)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For hanging block,&

$40 - T = 4a ⋯ \left(1\right)$

Now, maximum value of friction force will be,

${f}_\max = \muN = 0 . 02 \times40 \times10 = 8N$

For block on table,~$T - 8 = 40a ⋯ \left(2\right)$

From equation(1) and equation (2), we get$32 = 44a ⇒ a = \dfrac{32}{44} = \dfrac{8}{11}ms^{- 2}$& &

questions.q: A car of mass ' $m$ ' moves on a banked road having radius ' $r$ ' and banking angle $\theta$. To avoid slipping from banked road, the maximum permissible speed of the car is $v_0$. The coefficient of friction $\mu$ between the wheels of the car and the banked road is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: So, $N=m g \cos \theta+\frac{m v_0^2}{r} \sin \thetaf_r=\mu m g \cos \theta+\frac{\mu m v_0^2}{r} \sin \theta\begin{aligned} & \text { And } \frac{m v_0^2}{r} \cos \theta=m g \sin \theta+f_r \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{m v_0^2}{r} \cos \theta-m g \sin \theta=\mu\left(m g \cos \theta+\frac{m v_0^2}{r} \sin \theta\right) \\ & \Rightarrow\left(v_0^2-g r \tan \theta\right)=\mu\left(v_0^2 \tan \theta+g r\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \mu=\frac{v_0^2-g r \tan \theta}{g r+v_0^2 \tan \theta} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: The position vector of a particle related to time $t$ is given by~$\overset{→}{r} = \left(10t\overset{^}{i} + 15t^{2}\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}\right)m$.& The direction of net force experienced by the particle is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, the position vector of the particle is

$\overset{→}{r} = 10t\overset{^}{i} + 15t^{2}\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}$

The velocity of the particle can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}\overset{→}{v} & = & \dfrac{d\overset{→}{r}}{dt} \\ & = & \dfrac{d}{dt}\left(10t\overset{^}{i} + 15t^{2}\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}\right) \\ & = & 10\overset{^}{i} + 30t\overset{^}{j}\end{cases}$

And, the acceleration of the particle is given by

$\begin{cases}\overset{→}{a} & = & \dfrac{d\overset{→}{v}}{dt} \\ & = & \dfrac{d}{dt}\left(10\overset{^}{i} + 30t\overset{^}{j}\right) \\ & = & 30\overset{^}{j}\end{cases}$

Hence, the force on the particle can be written as

$\begin{cases}\overset{→}{F} & = & m\overset{→}{a} \\ & = & 30m\overset{^}{j}\end{cases}$

questions.q: A spring mass system (mass $m,$ spring constant $k$ and natural length $l$ ) rests in equilibrium on a horizontal disc. The free end of the spring is fixed at the centre of the disc. If the disc together with spring mass system rotates about it's axis with an angular velocity $\omega,  \left(k > > m{\omega}^{2}\right) the relative change in the length of the spring is best given by the option:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$m{\omega}^{2}\left({l}_{0} + x\right) = kx$
\left(\dfrac{{l}_{0}}{x} + 1\right) = \dfrac{k}{m{\omega}^{2}}$
$x = \dfrac{{l}_{0}m{\omega}^{2}}{k - m{\omega}^{2}}$
$k ≫ m{\omega}^{2}$
So, $\dfrac{x}{{l}_{0}}$ is equal to $\dfrac{m{\omega}^{2}}{k}$

$

questions.q: A $1 \mathrm{~kg}$ mass is suspended from the ceiling by a rope of length $4 \mathrm{~m}$. A horizontal force ' $F$ ' is applied at the mid point of the rope so that the rope makes an angle of $45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ with respect to the vertical axis as shown in figure. The magnitude of $F$ is : (Assume that the system is in equilibrium and $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{T}_1 \sin 45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=\mathrm{F} \\ & \mathrm{T}_1 \cos 45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=\mathrm{T}_2=1 \times \mathrm{g} \\ & \therefore \tan 45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{g}} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{F}=10 \mathrm{~N}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
A steel block of $10$ kg rests on a horizontal floor as shown. When three iron cylinders are placed on it as shown, the block and cylinders go down with an acceleration $0 . 2ms^{- 2} .$ The normal reaction $R^{'}$ by the floor if mass of the iron cylinders are equal and of $20$ kg each is \left(\text{in}N\right)$,

[Take $g = 10ms^{- 2}$ and \left{μ}_{s} = 0 . 2\right]$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Writing force equation in vertical direction,&
$Mg - N = Ma$
$⇒ 70g - N = 70 \times 0 . 2$
$⇒ N = 70 [ g - 0 . 2 ] = 70 \times 9 . 8$
$∴ N = 686$~newton
Note: Since there is no compressive normal from the sides, hence friction will not act.
Hence option~$2 .$

questions.q: A ball is released from rest from point $P$ of a smooth semi-spherical vessel as shown in figure. The ratio of the centripetal force and normal reaction on the ball at point $Q$ is $A$ while angular position of point $Q$ is $\alpha$ with respect to point $P$. Which of the following graphs represent the correct relation between $A$ and $\alpha$ when ball goes from $Q$ to $R$?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At angular position& $\alpha$~as shown in the figure, applying conservation of mechanical energy

$mgRsin\alpha = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} ⇒ \dfrac{mv^{2}}{R} = 2mgsin\alpha$

In the radial direction,

$N - mgsin\alpha = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{R} ⇒ N = 3mgsin\alpha$

Now the ratio of centripetal force and normal reaction is,

$A = \dfrac{mv^{2}R}{N} = \dfrac{2mgsin\alpha}{3mgsin\alpha} = \dfrac{2}{3}$.~ Therefore,~$A$& is constant.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: An elevator can go up or down with uniform speed when its weight is balanced with the tension of its cable.
Statement-II: Force exerted by the floor of an elevator on the foot of a person standing on it is more than his/her weight when the elevator goes down with increasing speed.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When elevator is moving with uniform speed $T = {F}_{g}$, as the net force along the vertical direction should be zero.

Therefore, Statement-I is true.

Now, when elevator is going down with increasing speed, its acceleration is downward.
Hence,~

$W - N = ma ⇒ W - N = \dfrac{W}{g} \times a$

$⇒ N = W \left($1 - \dfrac{a}{g}\right)$

Clearly, normal reaction is& less than weight. So Statement-II is false.

$

questions.q: A block of mass $m$ is kept on a platform which starts from rest with a constant acceleration $g / 2$ upwards, as shown in the figure. Work done by normal reaction on block in time $t$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$N - mg = \dfrac{mg}{2}$
$N = \dfrac{3mg}{2}$
$s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}$
$= 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{g}{2}t^{2}$
$= \dfrac{g}{4}t^{2}$
${W}_{N} = \dfrac{3mg}{2} \times \dfrac{g}{4}t^{2}$
$= \dfrac{3mg^{2}t^{2}}{8} = \dfrac{3mg^{2}t^{2}}{8}$

questions.q: The time taken by an object to slide down $45 °$ rough inclined plane is $n$ times as it takes to slide down a perfectly smooth $45 °$ incline plane. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the incline plane is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let angle of inclination is& $\theta = 45 °$.

Then, acceleration along the incline in case of smooth incline will be,~${a}_{1} = gsin\theta = \dfrac{g}{2}$.

In case of rough incline, kinetic friction will act against the direction of motion. Normal force acting on the object will be~$mgcos\theta$. Therefore,~acceleration along the incline in case of rough incline will be,

${a}_{2} = gsin\theta - \mugcos\theta = \dfrac{g}{2} - \dfrac{\mug}{2}$.

Now as per question,

${t}_{2} = n{t}_{1}$

and as the displacement covered is the same in both case,~$0 + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{1}{t}_{1}^{2} = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{2}{t}_{2}^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{g}{2}{t}_{1}^{2} = \left(\dfrac{g}{2} - \dfrac{\mug}{2}\right)n^{2}{t}_{1}^{2}$

$⇒ \mu = 1 - \dfrac{1}{n2}$

questions.q: A disc with a flat small bottom beaker placed on it at a distance $R$~from its center is revolving about an axis passing through the center and perpendicular to its plane with an angular velocity $\omega$. The coefficient of static friction between the bottom of the beaker and the surface of the disc is $\mu$. The beaker will revolve with the disc if :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As the disc is revolving in circular motion about an axis passing through centre& and perpendicular to its plane, thus centrifugal force must act on it. The forces acting on disc is shown below.

& From FBD

For circular motion,& frictional force must balance the required centripetal force.

So,& $f = m{ω}^{2}R$

$⇒ \muN \ge m{ω}^{2}R$

$⇒ \mumg \ge m{ω}^{2}R$

$⇒ R \le \dfrac{\mug}{\omega2}$

questions.q: A massless spring gets elongated by amount $x_1$ under a tension of 5 N . Its elongation is $x_2$ under the tension of 7 N . For the elongation of  \left(5 x_1-2 x_2\right)$, the tension in the spring will be$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{kx}_1=5 \mathrm{~N} \\ & \mathrm{kx}_2=7 \mathrm{~N} \\ & \mathrm{k}\left(5 \mathrm{x}_1-2 \mathrm{x}_2\right)=5 \mathrm{kx}_1-2 \mathrm{kx}_2 \\ & =5 \times 5-2 \times 7=11 \mathrm{~N}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A stone of mass $900g$ is tied to a string and moved in a vertical circle of radius $1m$ making $10$ rpm. The tension in the string, when the stone is at the lowest point is (if ${π}^{2} = 9 . 8$ and $g = 9 . 8ms^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given that

Given the mass $m = 900g = \dfrac{900}{1000}kg = \dfrac{9}{10}kg$,

The radius of the circular path $r = 1m$

And, the angular velocity

$\omega = \dfrac{2\pi N}{60} = \dfrac{2\pi ( 10 )}{60} = \dfrac{π}{3}rads^{- 1}$

With reference to the above diagram, the formula to calculate the tension at the lowermost point can be written as

$T - mg = mr{ω}^{2} ⇒ T = mg + mr{ω}^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

\begin{cases}$T & = & $\dfrac{9}{10} \times$9 . 8 + $\dfrac{9}{10} \ttimes$1 \left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right)2 \\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } 8 . 82 + \dfrac{9}{10} \times \dfrac{\pi2}{9}\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } 8 . 82 + 0 . 98 \\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } 9 . 8N\end{cases}

$

questions.q: A block $A$~takes $2s$ to slide down a frictionless incline of $30 °$ and length $l$, kept inside a lift going up with uniform velocity $v$. If the incline is changed to $45 °$, the time taken by the block, to slide down the incline, will be approximately:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$

As per the information given in the question the lift is moving upward with uniform velocity. Therefore, the frame of reference attached to the lift is an inertial frame of reference. The acceleration of the block down the incline will be,

$a = gsin\theta$

Using equation of motion for constant acceleration,

$s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}$

$⇒ l = \dfrac{1}{2}gsin30 ° \left(2\right)2 . . . \left($1\right)$

When the inclination is changed to~$45 °$,

$l = $\dfrac{1}{2}$gsin45 ° t^{2} . . . \left(2\right)$

Equating the above equations,

$\dfrac{1}{2}gsin30 ° \left(2\right)2 = \dfrac{1}{2}gsin45 ° \left(t\right)2$

$⇒ \$left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left($4\right) = $\dfrac{1}{2}$t^{2} ⇒ t = $\sqrt{2\sqrt{2}} =$1 . 68s$

questions.q: As shown in the figure a block of mass $10$ kg lying on a horizontal surface is pulled by a force F acting at an angle $30 °$, with horizontal. For ${μ}_{s} = 0 . 25$, the block will just start to move for the value of $F$: [Given g $= 10m \cdot s^{– 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The free body diagram for the given scenario is shown below-

From the equilibrium of the vertical component of forces, it can be written that

$\begin{cases}N & = & mg - Fsin30 ° \\ & = & mg - \dfrac{F}{2} \\ & = & 100 - \dfrac{F}{2} \\ & = & \dfrac{200 - F}{2} . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 1 )\end{cases}$

From the equilibrium of horizontal component of forces, it can be written that,

$Fcos30 ° = \muN . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ( 2 )$

Substitute the expression for the normal reaction force from equation (1) into equation (2) and solve to calculate the value of the applied force.

$\begin{cases}\sqrt{3}\dfrac{F}{2} & = & 0 . 25 \times \left(\dfrac{200 - F}{2}\right) \\ 4\sqrt{3}F & = & 200 - F \\ F & = & \dfrac{200}{4\sqrt{3} + 1} \\ & \approx & 25 . 2\end{cases}$

questions.q: A spring whose unstrentches length is $l$ has a force constant $k .$ The spring is cut into two pieces of unstretches lengths ${l}_{1}$ and ${l}_{2}$ where, ${l}_{1} = n{l}_{2}$ and $n$ is an integer. The ratio ${k}_{1} / {k}_{2}$ of the corresponding force constants, ${k}_{1}$ and ${k}_{2}$ will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Spring constants of the spring will be inversely proportional to length.
$\dfrac{{k}_{1}}{{k}_{2}} = \dfrac{{l}_{2}}{{l}_{1}} = \dfrac{1}{n}$

questions.q:
Statement I:& A cyclist is moving on an unbanked road with a speed of $7kmh^{- 1}$ and takes a sharp circular turn along a path of the radius of $2m$ without reducing the speed. The static friction coefficient is $0 . 2$. The cyclist will not slip and pass the curve \left(g = 9 . 8ms^{- 2}\right)$

Statement II : If the road is banked at an angle of $45 °$, cyclist can cross the curve of $2m$ radius with the speed of $18 . 5kmh^{- 1}$ without slipping. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

$
options: Statement I is incorrect and statement II is correct

Statement I is correct and statement II is
incorrect
Both statement I and statement II are false
Both statement I and statement II are true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Statement I${v}_\max = \sqrt{\muRg} = \sqrt{\left(0 . 2\right) \times 2 \times 9 . 8}$

${v}_\max = 1 . 97ms^{- 1}$

$7kmh^{- 1} = 1 . 944ms^{- 1}$

Speed is lower than ${v}_\max$, hence it can take safe
turn.

Statement II~

${v}_\max = \sqrt{Rg \left[\dfrac{tan \theta + \mu}{1 - \mu tan \theta}\right]}$

$= \sqrt{2 \times 9 . 8\left[\dfrac{1 + 0 . 2}{1 - 0 . 2}\right]} = 5 . 42ms^{- 1}$

$18 . 5kmh^{- 1} = 5 . 14ms^{- 1}$

Speed is lower than ${v}_\max$, hence it can take safe turn.

The angle made by upper half of the rope with vertical is $\alpha = \tan^{- 1} \left($x $\times {10}^{- 1}\right). The value of $x$ is _____ .

$
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: The length of a light string is 1.4 m when the tension on it is 5 N. If the tension increases to 7 N , the length of the string is 1.56 m. The original length of the string is _____ m.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{T}=\mathrm{K}\left(\ell-\ell_0\right) \\ & \Rightarrow 5=\mathrm{K}\left(1.4-\ell_0\right) \\ & \Rightarrow 7=\mathrm{K}\left(1.56-\ell_0\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{5}{1.4-\ell_0}=\frac{7}{1.56-\ell_0} \\ & \therefore \ell_0=1 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A block starts moving up an inclined plane of inclination $30 °$ with an initial velocity of${v}_{0}$. It comes back to its initial position with velocity $\dfrac{v0}{2} .$ The value of the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the inclined plane is close to $\dfrac{1}{1000},$ The nearest integer to $I$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$AtoB$

${a}_{1} = gsin30 ° + \mu gcos30 °$

$= \dfrac{g}{2} + \dfrac{\mu g\sqrt{3}}{2}; g = 10ms^{2}$

${v}_{0}^{2} - 2{a}_{1}\left(s\right) = 0$

$s = {v}_{0}^{2}{a}_{1}$~ ~ .....(i)

$BtoA$

${a}_{2} = \dfrac{g}{2} - \dfrac{\mu\sqrt{3}}{2}g$

\left(\dfrac{V0}{2}\right)2 = 2{a}_{2} \left(s\right)$

$s = {V}_{0}^{2}4{a}_{2}$~ .....(ii)

From equation (i) and (ii)

${V}_{0}^{2}{a}_{1} = {V}_{0}^{2}4{a}_{2}$

$⇒ {a}_{1} = 4{a}_{2}$

$⇒ 5 + $5\sqrt{3}\mu ==$4 \left\{5 - 5\sqrt{3}\mu\right\}$

$⇒ 5 + 5\sqrt{3}\mu⇒ 25\sqrt{3}\mu =15 ⇒ \mu = \dfrac{3}{5} =0 . 346 = \dfrac{346}{1000}$

So,~$\dfrac{1}{1000} = \dfrac{346}{1000}$&

$

questions.q: A particle is moving in a circle of radius $50$ cm in such a way that at any instant the normal and tangential components of its acceleration are equal. If its speed at $t = 0$ is $4ms^{- 1}$, the time taken to complete the first revolution will be $\dfrac{1}{α}\left[1 - e^{- 2\pi}\right]s$, where \alpha =______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:

\left|\overset{→}{a}c\right| = \left|\overset{→}{a}t\right|$

$⇒ \dfrac{v2}{r} = \dfrac{dv}{dt}$

$⇒ {∫}_{4}^{v}\dfrac{dv}{v2} = {∫}_{0}^{t}\dfrac{dt}{r}$

$⇒ {\dfrac{- 1}{v}}_{4}^{v} = \dfrac{t}{r}$

$⇒ \dfrac{- 1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{4} = 2t$

$⇒ v = \dfrac{4}{1 - 8t} = \dfrac{ds}{dt}$

$⇒ 4{∫}_{0}^{t}\dfrac{dt}{1 - 8t} = {∫}_{0}^{s}ds$

\left(r = 0 . 5m, \text{distance}\text{covered}s = 2\pir = \pi\right)$

$⇒ 4 \times \dfrac{[ ln ( 1 - 8t ) {]}_{0}^{t}}{- 8} = \pi$

$⇒ ℓn ( 1 - 8t ) = - 2\pi$

$⇒ 1 - 8t = e^{- 2\pi}$

$⇒ t = \left(1 - e^{- 2\pi}\right)\dfrac{1}{8}s$

So, $\alpha = 8.

$
